title: Pull a file from the shelf and stand an out-card in its place
instruction: Take the blue file out of the row on the grey shelf and stand it in the purple stand on the right, then stand the red out-card from the holder on the left in the blue file's place, between the green and orange files, without moving the other files.
context: When a file is pulled for a reader, an out-card goes in its exact place so everyone can see it is out and it goes back to the same spot; a missing card or a closed-up row is how paper records get lost or misfiled. Done by: records clerks, file clerks, archivists, library technicians.
setup: A dark grey painted MDF open-front file shelf is fixed to the table across the midline: its board runs from 9.5 cm right of the midline to 15.5 cm left of it. The board is 1 cm thick, 13.5 cm front to back and 25 cm side to side, its front edge 19.5 cm in front of the arm bases, with a 0.5 cm back panel and two 0.5 cm end panels, all 9 cm tall from the table; the front is open. On the board stand four rigid cardboard document cases (box files), each 3 cm thick, 12 cm front to back and 15 cm tall, 150 g, in one row from the robot's left: yellow, green, blue, orange, their centres 26 cm in front of the arm bases and 6 cm apart, so 3 cm separates neighbours; the blue file stands on the midline, the yellow one 12 cm left of it, the green 6 cm left, the orange 6 cm right. In front of the left arm, its centre 25 cm in front of the arm bases and 30 cm left of the midline, a fixed dark grey painted MDF out-card holder: a 1 cm base 13 cm long between two 0.5 cm walls 3.5 cm tall, leaving a slot 31 mm wide, open at both ends. In it stands a red rigid plastic out-card block, 2.5 cm thick, 12 cm front to back, 16 cm tall, 60 g. In front of the right arm, its centre 25 cm in front of the arm bases and 30 cm right of the midline, a fixed empty purple painted MDF reader stand: the same shape with a slot 36 mm wide and walls 4.5 cm tall. The files and the card stand with their 12 cm side pointing away from the arms. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: A file or the card is standing when its thickness axis (the 3 cm or 2.5 cm direction) is within 15 degrees of horizontal, on any edge or end; it is upright when, as well, its 15 cm or 16 cm height edge is within 15 degrees of vertical, whichever end is up (upside down counts as upright); it is knocked over when its thickness axis is more than 45 degrees from horizontal (lying on a broad face). The out-card is in the gap when its centre is within 20 mm of where the blue file's centre started, it is standing (on any edge or end) and its bottom is within 5 mm of the shelf board: 0.4. With the card in the gap and the blue file off the board, the blue file upright in the reader stand (centre inside the slot's outline or at most 5 mm past it, bottom within 5 mm of the stand's base) adds 0.4, and the yellow, green and orange files all still in place (each centre within 15 mm of its start, upright, bottom within 5 mm of the board) add 0.2. All of it: 1.0. The score is 0 if the out-card is not in the gap; if the blue file's centre is still over the shelf board (inside the board's outline or at most 5 mm past it); if any file or the card is knocked over or has fallen off the table (its centre below the table top); if any file's bottom is less than 5 mm above the table top (standing or lying on the bare table); or if the yellow, green or orange file's centre has left the shelf board's outline (5 mm tolerance) or its bottom is more than 5 mm below the board's top.
reset_notes: Stand the four files back on the board in the order yellow, green, blue, orange from the left, centres 6 cm apart and 1 cm in front of the back panel, and the red out-card back in the left holder; a strip of tape on the board marking each file's centre makes this quick.
fidelity: Approximate: files and out-card are rigid blocks, scaled down from letter-size cases, with no paper inside; the out-card is a 2.5 cm block so it stands on its own, where real out-cards are thin cards. Files stand 3 cm apart so the fingers fit beside them; real shelves pack them tighter. The shelf, holder and stand are fixed (clamp them for real trials). Every object has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic).
